Sovereign Lab / Understanding federation
SYNTHETIC LAB & DESIGN
Sovereign Federation Lab / Reader guide · edition 09

Why this lab exists.

Explore useful sharing across bank businesses without treating identity, access and location as the same decision.

Implemented lab

The synthetic container lab is validated. Technical extension points on this page remain proposals unless explicitly identified as implemented. Understand the labels.

Start with the example · Look up a term

The problem

A bank may serve one person through many legal entities. Useful sharing must coexist with independent business ownership, access restrictions and approved storage locations. A universal customer copy or a geography switch alone cannot express those boundaries.

What the demonstration answers

The lab shows approved minimal party identity, policy-scoped relationship data, source-side exclusions, acknowledged movement and a controlled India migration. Thirty synthetic entity mappings sit over three base stores; Mumbai is the fourth store for the isolated migration fixture.

What remains an evaluation

This is a single-host experiment, not a connected bank estate. Regional identity, HA, distributed authority, normalized-table migration and large-scale performance remain pilot work. The original flat-record generator remains a separate teaching example.

Follow the reader guide or inspect acceptance evidence.
